q1_code_mechanics.worker_assignment: lake_filler.py main(): diversity queue is a shared Python list `q` behind `qlock`; each of `a.workers` (currently 10, see q6 evidence) threads calls diversity_worker() which does `with qlock: item = q.pop(0)` -- one atomic pop per claim, so within ONE lake_filler.py process diversity workers cannot double-claim. Bulk workers get a static 1:1 assignment: `bulk = todo[-a.bulk_workers:]`, disjoint from `small = todo[:len(todo)-len(bulk)]`, so no overlap between diversity and bulk queues within one process either.
q1_code_mechanics.exit_code_origin: exit_code in filler-state.json is `p.returncode` from `subprocess.run([...,'modellake.py','acquire',...])` in lake_filler.fetch(). modellake.py main() computes its own return code as `0 if out.get('acquired', ...) is not False else 1` -- so ANY unsuccessful acquire() outcome (capacity refusal, hf-download nonzero/negative return, hash rejection) surfaces as parent exit_code=1. A truly uncaught Python exception (e.g. the ValueError modellake.acquire() raises on revision mismatch) also exits 1 by CPython default, and neither modellake.py nor lake_filler.py contains a single `try`/`except` anywhere (grep returned zero matches in both files) -- ruled out the 'broad except disguises a real error' trap this campaign hit before; there is no except block here to disguise anything.
q1_code_mechanics.bytes_on_disk_measurement: lake_filler.fetch() computes `got = ml.du(ml.TIER2 / item['slug'])` AFTER the subprocess exits -- i.e. it measures only the FINAL published directory under specimens/, which modellake.acquire() populates via `os.rename(part, final)` and ONLY after every declared file passes sha256 (or size-only) verification. bytes_on_disk=0 therefore means the atomic rename never happened; it does NOT mean zero network bytes were transferred -- partial data can exist under partial/<slug>/ and never be counted.
q1_code_mechanics.can_two_workers_claim_same_repo: Within a single lake_filler.py run: no (qlock + disjoint index ranges, see above). ACROSS processes: yes, nothing stops it. plan() de-dupes only against `resident_slugs()` (specimens/ directories that are FULLY published) at the single moment plan() runs; there is no in-progress claim registry, lock file, or PID file anywhere in either script. This is not hypothetical -- see q4/live evidence below: two live OS processes are right now both running `modellake.py acquire --repo moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct --revision e1df551a447157d4658b573f9a695d57658590e9` against the identical target path.
